definition: The fideistic interpretation of the later Wittgenstein: religion as a self-contained enterprise governed by its own internal grammar (Nielsen's label, 1967). Three variants are kept apart: WF-N, the critics' characterization with its four theses (cut off, self-referential, intelligible only to believers, not criticizable); WF-P1, the early Phillips (religious belief as the expression of a moral vision; praise of God does not refer to some object called God); WF-P2, the later Phillips and religious minimalism (reference and truth constituted inside the religious game, outside evidence admissible). It is not a view attributed to Wittgenstein.
